methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A community-wide AI readiness initiative in Roanoke signals intentional capacity-building beyond NoVA, but success depends on whether this creates deep implementation capability or remains at the strategic planning level without distributed technical fluency.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Local backlash forcing Amazon to scrap four data centers reveals that infrastructure concentration without community buy-in creates political friction that could slow NoVA's AI growth while regions building strategic capacity (like Roanoke) gain competitive advantage through stakeholder alignment.

signals.title: Norfolk, Newport News police launch AI tool for non-emergency calls - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk and Newport News deploying turnkey AI tools for non-emergency calls demonstrates shallow but distributed adoption—platform-delivered capability that spreads geographically without building deep local AI development expertise or creating transferable technical skills.

signals.title: Military spouse uses AI to help veterans navigate VA benefits - DC Military
signals.signal_reading: A military spouse independently building AI tools to navigate VA benefits exemplifies grassroots, peer-driven capability development outside institutional channels—precisely the distributed, deep fluency that could emerge from personal necessity rather than corporate or academic concentration.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: A statewide gubernatorial order on AI cybersecurity centralizes policy response at the state level but signals concentration of AI governance expertise in Richmond without evidence of distributed implementation capacity across regional governments or rural jurisdictions.
